meta.label: Tablets
meta.attribution: Options are specific tablet models on sale in October 2026 in the US, UK and EU. Since June 2025 every smartphone and slate tablet sold in the EU must carry an energy label and a public record in the EU product register (EPREL, eprel.ec.europa.eu), and that record is the main source here. Repairable: the EU repairability index (0 to 5, built from disassembly depth, fasteners, tools, spare parts, repair information and software updates) times 20; for a model outside the register, iFixit's teardown score out of 10 times 10, noted where used. Long support: the minimum years of security and operating-system updates the maker declares in the register, counted from when the model stops being sold in the EU (5 years scores 70, 6 scores 80, 7 scores 90); for a model outside the register, the maker's own published support date, scored on the same rough scale. Durable: from the same EU record, the battery's rated charge cycles (800 cycles scores 50, 1,000 scores 60, 1,200 scores 70, 2,000 scores 90), plus 10, 7, 5 or 2 points for drop-test class A, B, C or D, plus 5 for IP68 dust and water protection. Price: the maker's own store on the date checked, base configuration where it could be identified, in that store's currency; bands treat dollars and pounds at face value (150 or less scores 95, up to 200 scores 88, 300 scores 80, 400 scores 72, 500 scores 64, 650 scores 56, 800 scores 48, 1,000 scores 40, 1,300 scores 30, above that 20). Sale prices are noted. Not scored: privacy, which depends mostly on the operating system and accounts rather than the tablet model and has no per-model independent test; screen and performance; energy class. The Google Pixel Tablet is left out because the Google Store no longer sells it, OnePlus because it ended new product rollouts in Europe and North America in 2026, and Amazon's new Alexa Tablets because, at launch, Amazon had published no update period and no repair data existed yet. Sources: EPREL records, iFixit's tablet repairability table, Apple, Samsung, Lenovo, Microsoft and Amazon store and support pages, Microsoft's Surface lifecycle table, Amazon's Fire tablet security update page. The greenest tablet is usually the one you already own. Reviewed 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Apple iPad (A16)
products.description: Apple's entry iPad from 2025: long update history, but glued construction and a middling EU repair score.

repairability.note: The EU energy label record for the Apple iPad (A16) (model A3354, EPREL 2261043) gives a repairability index of 2.78 out of 5, class C, and lists spare-part availability for the display; scored here as the index times 20.

durability.note: The same EU label record rates the battery for 1000 full charge cycles and says the Apple iPad (A16) declares no passed drop test, reliability class E, with an IP42 rating for dust and water.

longevity.note: The maker declares in the EU register that the Apple iPad (A16) will get security and operating-system updates for at least 5 years after the model stops being sold in the EU.

economical.note: Apple's US store lists the iPad (A16) from $449 on the date checked.

products.name: Microsoft Surface Pro (2026)
products.description: A Windows 2-in-1 rather than a mobile-OS tablet; Microsoft publishes service guides and sells parts, and iFixit scores the line well.

repairability.note: iFixit's tablet repairability table gives the Surface Pro 11 (2024), the predecessor of the current models, 8 out of 10 for a rear storage hatch, a screwed-in battery, public repair manuals and spare parts; Microsoft's current Surface Pro page says replacement components are sold through the Microsoft Store and iFixit. The Surface Pro has no record in the EU label register, so the iFixit score is used, times 10.

longevity.note: Microsoft's Surface lifecycle table lists driver and firmware support for the Surface Pro 12th Edition (Snapdragon) from June 16, 2026 to June 16, 2032, and for the Surface Pro 12-inch 2nd Edition from October 13, 2026 to October 13, 2032: six years from release.

economical.note: Microsoft's US store lists the Surface Pro 12-inch from $1,149.99, keyboard sold separately.

products.name: Amazon Fire HD 10 (2023)
products.description: The cheap Fire OS tablet many households already own, still sold in the US; Amazon's new Android-based Alexa Tablets replace the line from October 2026.

longevity.note: Amazon's Fire tablet security page says it will provide security updates 'until at least four years from when you bought it new, from Amazon as the seller' and lists the Fire HD 10 (Generation 13, 2023) as supported at least through 31 December 2029. It is not in the EU label register, so no repair or durability figures are scored.

economical.note: Amazon's US listing for the Fire HD 10 (32 GB) showed $154.99 and in stock on the date checked.
